transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhao (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dr. Laura Kim (CTO - Vanguard Clinic), Marcus Reed (Head of Eng), Anita Shah (DevOps), Oliver Park (PM)

Summary:
Quick onboarding/kickoff for Vanguard Clinic to review onboarding plan, security/compliance needs, pilot scope (EHR redaction + triage), timeline for pilot, and action items to start pilot next week. Customer has strict PHI handling needs and wants private deployment conversation and dedicated capacity options.

Agenda/Topics:
- Introductions and roles
- Current stack and constraints (EHR vendor, data residency)
- Security/compliance review (SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs)
- Deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC)
- Pilot scope, success criteria, timeline
- Next steps and responsibilities

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Sofia, your AE, with Ethan from CS and Priya our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Dr. Laura Kim: Hi Sofia, thanks. busy but good. excited to get this started.
[00:00:20] Marcus Reed: morning all. we've got a few people from infra and product here so we can cover questions.
[00:00:29] Sofia Martinez: Great. Agenda is pretty short — we want to run through the onboarding plan, understand your constraints especially around PHI, discuss deployment options, and align on pilot scope and timeline. Priya, wanna take the tech deck for a minute?
[00:00:45] Priya Nair: Sure. So high level Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments — VPC or on-prem if you need air-gapped. For pilot most customers start on a Dedicated pool for predictable throughput, then consider private if data residency or managed KMS is required.
[00:01:05] Anita Shah: Just to be clear — anything touching PHI needs to be encrypted at rest with our KMS and audit logs retained for 12 months. We also use Okta for SSO.
[00:01:18] Ethan Zhao: Totally understood. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and integrates with common SSO providers (SAML/Okta). We log token-level access and can provide the audit export for compliance. We'll share the SOC 2 and security whitepaper after this call.
[00:01:34] Oliver Park: timeline wise, we're aiming for a 6 week pilot and then a phased rollout. we'd like to see latency under 300ms p50 for short prompts and cost metrics before expanding.
[00:01:46] Priya Nair: For latency targets, we typically recommend a model profile + batching config. If you want 300ms p50 with PHI-safe redaction we can run a small benchmark on Dedicated. There's also quantized variants to reduce cost.
[00:02:05] Marcus Reed: what's the difference operationally between Dedicated and private VPC? cost and management overhead?
[00:02:12] Priya Nair: Dedicated is Redwood-managed hardware reserved for you — we handle updates, autoscaling, maintenance; Private VPC gives you control over networking and can be deployed inside your cloud account or on-prem, which increases operational responsibility but keeps data inside your VPC. Cost is usually higher for private due to infra + entitlements.
[00:02:31] Dr. Laura Kim: And for audit — do you store request text? we need guarantees around retention and deletion.
[00:02:39] Ethan Zhao: By default hosted requests may be stored for observability, but for Dedicated and Private we offer zero-retention modes and customer-managed keys. We'll include specific retention options in the security doc.
[00:02:50] Marcus Reed: ok good. also curious about fallback behaviour if dedicated capacity hits limits — will requests fall back to hosted?
[00:02:58] Priya Nair: We support smart routing policies. You can opt-in to automatic fallback to hosted compatible variants, or set strict routing to prevent cross-tenant routing for compliance reasons. We can demo the policy behavior during the SE deep-dive.
[00:03:14] Anita Shah: On networking — we use restrictive egress. if we do private VPC, what's required from our side?
[00:03:22] Priya Nair: For private VPC we need peering or private link config; we'll provide a checklist (CIDR ranges, required ports, subnets). If on-prem we'll coordinate with your infra team for an appliance or containerized runtime.
[00:03:36] Sofia Martinez: Quick qualification: what's your expected qps and typical sequence lengths? helps us size the Dedicated pool.
[00:03:44] Marcus Reed: initial pilot is low qps — maybe 5-10 rps, peak 25, sequences usually 128 tokens or less for triage.
[00:03:54] Priya Nair: That maps well to a small dedicated pool. We'll propose batching + prefix caching to help cost.
[00:04:02] Oliver Park: Success criteria for pilot are: integration with our EHR redaction pipeline, <300ms p50, PHI retention controls, and cost below $0.02 per 1k tokens (ballpark).
[00:04:16] Ethan Zhao: Great. We'll capture that as the pilot success criteria in the playbook.
[00:04:22] Dr. Laura Kim: One ask — we need SAML SSO and RBAC so product teams can access logs but not data.
[00:04:29] Priya Nair: Redwood supports RBAC and audit trails; we can map Okta groups to roles. We'll walk through the mapping during SE session.
[00:04:38] Marcus Reed: any concerns about model hallucination when used on EHR triage? we need deterministic redaction for PHI.
[00:04:46] Priya Nair: For PHI redaction we recommend a pre-filtering step with deterministic rules before any LLM. Redwood can host the model inference behind that filter; we also support structured output with function/tool calling so outputs are constrained. We'll add evals for hallucination detection to the quality monitoring.
[00:05:02] Sofia Martinez: ok practical items — we'll send the onboarding playbook, security docs, and a pricing sheet. Priya will set up a deep-dive to run a benchmark on a dedicated instance; Marcus will provide sample data staging details.
[00:05:15] Marcus Reed: Confirmed. we'll share an S3 bucket with sandbox data (PHI redacted) and add your se account; also I'll share our SSO admin.
[00:05:25] Anita Shah: retention: 12 months audit logs and 30 days request contents unless zero-retention is enabled. can you support both?
[00:05:32] Ethan Zhao: Yes; we support configurable retention policies and will document steps to enable zero-retention for sensitive endpoints.
[00:05:40] Dr. Laura Kim: ok timeline — can we start the pilot next week? we'd like to start ingest + a small test run by Dec 3.
[00:05:47] Priya Nair: We can spin up a dedicated pool in 48-72 hours after contract + infra details. For next week we can do the SE deep-dive and demo with a small benchmark run.
[00:05:58] Sofia Martinez: Perfect. Any blockers on the contract/legal side?
[00:06:02] Oliver Park: Procurement has some standard NHS-like addenda for data processing; legal will want to review the DPA.
[00:06:09] Ethan Zhao: We'll route the DPA and standard addendum template — I'll flag legal to share the docs.
[00:06:15] Sofia Martinez: Great. Any other questions?
[00:06:20] (short silence)
[00:06:24] Marcus Reed: Not from my side. Looking forward to the deep-dive.
[00:06:28] Dr. Laura Kim: same.
[00:06:30] Sofia Martinez: Ok recap of next steps then — I'll send playbook and pricing by Monday, Ethan will share SOC2 and security whitepaper, Priya will schedule the SE deep-dive and bench run, Marcus will share data + SSO contact. We'll reconvene after the bench run.
[00:06:47] Priya Nair: I'll include a checklist for VPC/private deploy in the invite; if you want a private demo we can include network folks.
[00:06:55] Anita Shah: please include required IP ranges and ports.
[00:06:58] Priya Nair: noted.
[00:07:00] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the docs referenced (onboarding playbook, security whitepaper, benchmark template).
[00:07:08] Marcus Reed: thanks, bye.
[00:07:10] Dr. Laura Kim: thanks, bye.

Notes & Artifacts referenced:
- Onboarding playbook (will be shared)
- Security whitepaper & SOC2 report (Ethan to share link)
- Benchmark spreadsheet template (SE to send)
- Pilot checklist & retention options (in playbook)

End of call.
